question: Should an explicit `CodexBarCLI cookie refresh --provider grok` be trusted to cross the Chrome browser-cookie and Keychain-prompt boundary without requiring `CODEXBAR_ALLOW_BROWSER_COOKIE_IMPORT=1`?
rationale: The implementation is designed to keep background and ordinary CLI work gated, but the acceptable scope of an explicit CLI action is a repository-level privacy and interaction-policy choice rather than a purely mechanical correctness question.

options.title: Approve explicit refresh import
options.body: Accept the documented rule that only the app, an explicit user-initiated refresh, or the environment override may import browser cookies.

options.title: Keep environment-only CLI imports
options.body: Require the environment override for all CLI browser-cookie imports, preserving the previous stricter command-line boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve explicit refresh import
recommendation.body: Accept the documented rule that only the app, an explicit user-initiated refresh, or the environment override may import browser cookies.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository ownership is the only concrete routing signal available for this browser-Keychain policy decision.
